Books, art & history

Six aviation books for six different readers

A visual history, a reference book and an interview guide are very different gifts. Match the subject to the reader; assigned training books should be confirmed with the instructor.

The picks

Chosen for the recipient and use described, using published product information. We have not hands-on tested these products.

  1. 1. Readers interested in aviation art and WWII history

    Bomber Boys: WWII Flight Jacket Art

    Photography of original flight jackets connects design, aircraft crews and personal history.

    Keep in mind
    The premium coffee-table format is a larger purchase than a paperback memoir.
    Before you choose
    Check format and shelf space; this is visual history rather than flight instruction.
    $129.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗
  2. 2. Students and curious aviation readers

    ASA Dictionary of Aeronautical Terms, 8th edition

    A reference organized around aviation terminology can help a reader look up unfamiliar language.

    Keep in mind
    A reference book is less of a leisure read than a narrative history.
    Before you choose
    Confirm the eighth edition and whether the recipient prefers print or digital references.
    $29.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗
  3. 3. Pilots interested in decision-making and performance

    ASA Human Factors

    Focuses on the human side of aviation rather than another equipment manual.

    Keep in mind
    A technical subject and higher book price make it best for an explicitly interested reader.
    Before you choose
    Confirm the required edition if it is for a course; it does not replace that course.
    $71.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗
  4. 4. Pilots who specifically want aviation-safety reading

    The Killing Zone, Paul A. Craig

    Accident analysis offers a serious topic for a pilot interested in risk and judgment.

    Keep in mind
    The subject can feel ominous as a celebratory gift; ask before choosing it.
    Before you choose
    Check edition and format with the reader, especially for assigned reading.
    $21.99Listed 2026-10-21 · Unavailable when checkedView at Pilot Mall↗
  5. 5. Students whose instructor recommends this book

    The Student Pilot’s Flight Manual, 12th edition

    A structured print manual is useful when it matches the school’s approach.

    Keep in mind
    Unrequested textbooks can duplicate or conflict with an existing course.
    Before you choose
    Confirm the twelfth edition with the instructor before purchasing.
    $44.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗
  6. 6. Pilots preparing for airline interviews

    Checklist for Success, 8th edition

    A focused interview-preparation book matches a specific career milestone.

    Keep in mind
    Not a general flying manual and unlikely to interest a casual enthusiast.
    Before you choose
    Confirm edition and relevance to the recipient’s interview process.
    $17.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗

How to choose

Check the recipient’s shelves before choosing a familiar title. Use the linked publisher pages to confirm authors, editions, and available formats. These are reading gifts; historical accounts and older technical discussions should not be presented as current flight instruction or substitutes for training.

Prices and availability can change. Check the exact model, delivered total and return terms with the seller. Our recommendations are researched editorial selections, not hands-on test results.
